scope: Proposition 2.7 (Conditional next-pin kernel) of the manuscript “Bloch's Law for Finite-Range Heisenberg Ferromagnets in Three Dimensions” (preprints/Blochs-Law-for-Finite-Range-Heisenberg-Ferromagnets-in-Three-Dimensions-October-5-2026/bloch-law-heisenberg.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 271 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4884bc0984dfd0f6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let V = I ⊔ B be a finite set with I ̸= ∅. Suppose a random permutation matrix Π satisfies (2.12), and let K = EΠ. Let GI be the event that every cycle meets I. On GI, let Σ be the column-forward permutation matrix on I giving the next positive visit to I. Then Pr(GI) = det(I − KBB). (2.13) If this probability is positive, then KBB is transient and E[Σ | GI] = KII + KIB(I − KBB)−1 KBI. (2.14) The right-hand side is the first positive I-hitting kernel of the Markov chain with independent transitions according to K. If B is empty, the determinant is one and the correction is zero.
